description.narrative:
Stakeholder effects: Increased access to climate finance (green building developers). The proposed Project will support access to climate finance, leveraging TUHFs market position in inner cities of South Africa. The climate finance portfolio is expected to be accompanied by GHG emission reductions.
Stakeholder Effects: Increased access to housing finance. The Project will support access to affordable housing finance. South Africa is rapidly urbanizing, and an estimated 26 percent of the urban population lives in informal housing areas. The Project will increase the supply of housing finance for the affordable housing segment in South Africa.
Contribution to Market Creation: Sustainability. IFC anticipates that its systematic engagement at both the sectoral and financial institutions levels, through investments, upstream, and advisory services, will help scale-up climate finance, strengthen green finance standards in the country, and encourage replication by other institutions in South Africa; thus, contributing towards increased environmental sustainability through the demonstration and capacity building channels.

The proposed project consists of an IFC investment of up to ZAR 960 million with a 7-year tenor in the senior tranche of a ZAR 1.2 billion special purpose vehicle (SPV), to be setup and sponsored by TUHF Holdings Limited, South Africa (TUHF or the Company). TUHF and a third-party investor will each invest ZAR 120 million in the junior and mezzanine tranches, respectively. The SPV will utilize the proceeds to finance the development of affordable EDGE-certified green residential buildings in South Africa. The Project is expected to be supported by the Market Accelerator for Green Construction (MAGC) Program as described in the Blended Finance Section.
